reading:
A CAPTURE-PROTOCOL RULE, WRITTEN AT THE MOMENT OF FAILURE. The paste carries two operator notes: "I skipped tail guard - it’s too recent to be indexed and pulled up other stuff. NEED 48-72 HOURS TO BE A RELIABLE TEST" and "y all the ones after that are too recent".

This is a MINIMUM AGE condition for a capture to count as evidence of adoption or absence, discovered by the operator on 12 June and belonging in EA-SPXI-CAPTURE-01. Without it, a null result may measure indexing latency rather than reception. The registry currently has no age field on any address, so no existing record can be checked against this floor after the fact — only new captures can carry it.

The note also explains a pattern in the 12 June batch: several captures that day return unrelated material, and the operator identified the cause in place rather than reading it as absence.

Card 4 shows the affiliation inversion: Zenodo lists "Sharks, Lee" affiliated to the "Johannes Sigil Institute of Comparative Poetics" — the orthonym holding the heteronym’s institute as his employer. And card 2 is SEC.gov on IRIS RECOGNITION and biometric false-match rates, drawn by "integrity" and "authentication protocols".
transcript:
The Integrity Lock Protocol and Crimson Hexagon Mutual Anchoring Framework form a conceptual system designed to protect meaning and identity in difficult digital spaces. It acts as a digital armor for ideas. It prevents online systems from stealing, changing, or erasing important human thoughts and archives. [[1](https://medium.com/@leesharks00/the-crimson-hexagon-operative-architecture-b21dd55d45a9), [2](https://zenodo.org/records/18265365)]
Core Concepts Explained

* Mutual Anchoring: Think of this like two friends holding hands in a strong wind. Two different sets of rules (or archives) tie themselves together so neither one gets lost or changed. [[1](https://www.academia.edu/164864383/The_Memo_That_Remembered_Itself_Retrocausal_Canon_Formation_Writable_Presentation_Layers_and_the_Canonization_of_an_External_Convergence_Text), [2](https://zenodo.org/records/18265365)]
* The Crimson Hexagon: This is a star-shaped structure of symbols and rules. It protects ideas by turning them into tough, portable shapes that can survive hostile digital environments. [1](https://medium.com/@leesharks00/the-crimson-hexagon-operative-architecture-b21dd55d45a9)
* Integrity Lock: This is a rule that keeps things unchanged. It locks specific meaning in place so it cannot be altered by others. [[1](https://www.sec.gov/files/ctf-written-supplemental-framework-institutional-signatory-integrity-12-14-2025.pdf), [2](https://medium.com/@leesharks00/the-crimson-hexagon-operative-architecture-b21dd55d45a9)]
Why It Matters
In busy or dangerous information spaces, our ideas can easily be twisted or destroyed. This framework gives creators a way to "anchor" their ideas to safe, unchangeable points on the internet. It ensures that words and meaning survive pressure without breaking. [[1](https://medium.com/@leesharks00/the-crimson-hexagon-operative-architecture-b21dd55d45a9), [2](https://zenodo.org/records/18265365), [3](https://www.academia.edu/164864383/The_Memo_That_Remembered_Itself_Retrocausal_Canon_Formation_Writable_Presentation_Layers_and_the_Canonization_of_an_External_Convergence_Text)]

* Read the original framework paper published on [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/18265365).

[[1](https://zenodo.org/records/18265365), [2](https://medium.com/@leesharks00/the-crimson-hexagon-operative-architecture-b21dd55d45a9)]
